metadata.sourceSummary: Built from the brand discovery conversation, current Grass project inspection, and focused local-market research.

brandCore.name: The Lawn Guy
brandCore.oneSentencePitch: Modern lawn care in Bradford for homeowners who want a sharp, clean yard without making lawn work their problem.
brandCore.positioningStatement: The Lawn Guy Bradford is a Bradford/BWG-only lawn care service led by Remy, built around reliable mowing, clean finishing details, friendly communication, and simple quote visits.
brandCore.mission: Help busy local homeowners and property managers keep their lawns clean, sharp, and easy to enjoy.
brandCore.vision: Become the trusted local lawn person clients return to year after year for mowing-first yard care in Bradford West Gwillimbury.
brandCore.brandPromise: A clean finish, friendly service, and a simple path from first text to maintained lawn.
brandCore.memoryHook: Quality, aesthetics, and customer service from a local owner who keeps the process simple.

localFacts.fact: Bradford West Gwillimbury had a 2021 Census population of 42,880 and 13,415 occupied private dwellings.
The Town of Bradford West Gwillimbury Clean Yards By-law requires weeds or turf grass over 20 cm / 7.8 inches to be trimmed or cut.
localFacts.source: Town of Bradford West Gwillimbury Clean Yards By-law 2012-025

marketPattern: Local competitors commonly emphasize reliability, professional care, free quotes, weekly mowing, fertilization, seasonal cleanups, insurance, and broad service areas.
Many competitors serve several nearby towns rather than Bradford only.
The clearest opening is a modern, personal, Bradford-only mowing-first brand with fast text communication and polished visual proof.

primaryAudience: Property managers with lawn maintenance needs
Adults who do not have the time, ability, interest, or equipment for yard work
secondaryAudience: People with overgrown or neglected lawns
People physically challenged by yard work
Homeowners unhappy with their current lawn-care provider
Residents who want help before grass or weeds become a by-law issue
secretHopes: They want to arrive home and feel relieved by a clean yard.
They want the lawn to look cared for without needing to think about every detail.
They want simple communication and no confusing sales process.
likelyObjections: No public review base at launch
whereToReachThem: Flyers and cards in Bradford neighbourhoods
Word of mouth after great visits

included: Quick quality check before leaving when possible
defaultMowStandard.fallback: 48-hour fix window when a legitimate issue is raised after the visit

activeLaunchServices.name: Lawn mowing
activeLaunchServices.notes: The most important offer and the recurring revenue base.

activeLaunchServices.name: Trimming and edging
activeLaunchServices.notes: Usually bundled with mowing as part of the clean finish.

activeLaunchServices.name: Leaf cleanup
activeLaunchServices.notes: Promote in fall and for neglected yards.

activeLaunchServices.name: Seasonal cleanup
activeLaunchServices.notes: Good for one-off clients and future mowing conversion.

activeLaunchServices.name: Seeding and fertilizing
activeLaunchServices.notes: Position as lawn improvement and seasonal care, with product use following label and legal requirements.

activeLaunchServices.name: Garden maintenance
activeLaunchServices.notes: Light garden upkeep only; avoid sounding like full landscaping.

conditionalOrHiddenServices.name: Pesticide-style weed control
conditionalOrHiddenServices.reason: Ontario commercial pesticide application has licensing requirements unless an exemption clearly applies.

conditionalOrHiddenServices.name: Grub and pest control
conditionalOrHiddenServices.reason: Pest-control treatments can trigger the same commercial pesticide/exterminator rules.

conditionalOrHiddenServices.name: Major landscaping
conditionalOrHiddenServices.reason: The brand should not sound like a full landscaping company at launch.

conditionalOrHiddenServices.name: Snow or winter service
conditionalOrHiddenServices.reason: The chosen seasonal scope is spring, summer, and fall.

quoteModel.publicPricing: No public price list at launch
quoteModel.firstAppointmentQuote: Verbal quote during the visit plus text summary afterward
quoteModel.futureQuoteDelivery: Text summary with scope and price

customerResponsibilities: Provide access instructions if gates or locked areas are involved.
Tell Remy about hazards, hidden obstacles, or sensitive areas.
offerStrategy.weatherPolicy: If rain or unsafe lawn conditions make service a poor idea, reschedule soon instead of forcing a bad cut.

positioning.category: Local lawn care and lawn mowing
positioning.fitOrDisrupt: Fit the lawn-care category while making the website and customer experience feel more modern than the local norm.
doCompareTo: A clean, simple mowing and yard-care provider
positioning.reasonToChooseNow: The yard needs care now, Remy serves Bradford directly, and the quote process is simple: text, visit, clear scope, clean finish.

voiceAndMessaging.pointOfView: First person owner-led where helpful: I, me, my, Remy.
voiceAndMessaging.homepageSupport: Sharp cuts, clean edges, and simple quote visits for Bradford lawns that need a better finish.

messagePillars.meaning: The customer should feel the job is handled without friction.
messagePillars.sampleCopy: Text me, show me the yard, and I will give you a clear quote.

messagePillars.meaning: Quality is shown through cut lines, edges, cleanup, and respect for the property.
messagePillars.sampleCopy: Cut, trim, blow, and check the finish before I leave.

messagePillars.meaning: The service area is narrow on purpose.
messagePillars.sampleCopy: Built for Bradford lawns, not a giant service map.

messagePillars.meaning: The brand feels polished online but human in communication.
messagePillars.sampleCopy: A clean modern site, a real local owner, and simple text updates.

copyRules: Prefer concrete service language over vague claims.
Do not overload visitors with technical lawn-care details.
Do not claim insurance, reviews, licensing, or guarantees that are not true yet.
Do not lead with age; use age only in the owner story if it helps make the brand human.
Treat early visuals as mockups or examples until real client photos exist.

visualIdentity.direction: Turf + Charcoal with high-tech yard app polish

brandDark.role: Deep green for contrast and symbol work

grass.role: Lawn energy, motion, and before/after visuals

sunAccent.role: Small highlights only; quote buttons, progress, and attention points

surface.role: Cards, forms, modals, and clean content surfaces

typography.primary: Geist or a similar clean sans-serif
typography.accent: Fraunces or another organic editorial accent
typography.guidance: Use clean sans for most UI and copy. Use the accent font for selected headlines, not long paragraphs. Avoid hard-to-read handwritten type in functional areas.

logoDirection.feel: Clean vector icon, modern and local, with cut-line or blade-like negative space.

imagery.style: Clear before/after lawn visuals, service-detail graphics, close crops of clean edges, and owner-led local proof.
rules: Use real photos as soon as possible.
Customer yard photos require permission and should not reveal addresses.
Mockups are acceptable before proof exists but should not pretend to be completed client work.
Avoid dark, blurry, generic stock-style lawns when a visitor needs to inspect the result.

motion.level: Showpiece on desktop, lighter on mobile
principles: Motion should reveal service value, not decorate randomly.
Use scroll and pointer interaction to show before/after transformation, cut lines, and service progression.

experience.before: The customer feels overwhelmed or unsatisfied by their current lawn.
experience.during: The customer feels confident, comfortable, and clear on what is happening.
experience.after: The customer feels pleased, satisfied, and proud to come home.
experience.buyingExperience: Text-first, short, personal, and clear. The website warms the lead, then the quote visit closes the details.
experience.supportExperience: Friendly, calm, and practical. A quote-helper chatbot can collect basics, but real quote handoff should push to text or email.

topicsToCover: How to prepare for a visit
topicsToAvoid: Irrelevant topics outside lawn and light yard care

community.futureCommunityTheme: People who care about clean, better-looking yards in Bradford.

launchProof: Visual mockups until real proof exists
Permission-based before/after photos as soon as possible
trustAndProof.reviewStrategy: Ask for a review after a great visit, not before trust is earned.
trustAndProof.photoPolicy: Ask permission before using yard photos and avoid showing addresses.

values.qualityDefinition: High standards throughout the project, with visible care in the cut, edges, cleanup, communication, and final check.
values.authenticityDefinition: Be real about the business stage, the owner, the service area, and what is or is not offered.

complianceGuardrails.pesticideAndHerbicideRule: Do not advertise paid pesticide, herbicide, weed-control, grub-control, or pest-control treatment unless the required Ontario licensing and product-label requirements are confirmed.
complianceGuardrails.fiestaHerbicideNote: Fiesta Herbicide should be treated as a regulated pesticide/herbicide context for commercial service copy. Owning the product is not enough to make paid commercial application claims safe.
allowedLaunchWording: Weed concerns can be discussed during the quote visit
Seeding and fertilizing available where appropriate
Lawn improvement services are quoted after seeing the yard
disallowedLaunchWording: Safe for kids and pets after 1 hour

practicalConstraints.timeline: Customer-driven; website should be ready to support incoming quote requests.
